## Circular to Licensed Corporations and Associated Entities

## Proper segregation and safeguarding of client money

This circular is issued for the purpose of reminding Licensed Corporations and Associated Entities of their obligations in relation to client money received or held in Hong Kong. The term  "client  money"  is  defined  in  Part  1  of  Schedule  1  to  the  Securities  and  Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) ("SFO").

Licensed Corporations and, to a lesser extent, Associated Entities may receive client money in a variety of circumstances, for example, when a client settles the purchase consideration of securities or when securities are sold on behalf of a client or when dividends are received on a client's behalf.

Licensed  Corporations  and  Associated  Entities  are  required  to  hold  and  deal  with  client money in the manner prescribed by the Securities and Futures (Client Money) Rules ("the Rules"). Licensed Corporations and Associated Entities are reminded that section 4(4) of the Rules  requires  them  within  1  business  day  of  receiving  client  money  to  pay  it  (a)  into  a segregated  account,  (b)  to  the  client,  or  (c)  in  accordance  with  the  written  direction  or standing  authority  of  the  client.  There  are  no  other  options.  Any  client  money  held  in  a segregated account must be retained there until paid out in accordance with section 5 of the Rules (a) to the client, (b) in accordance with the written direction or standing authority of the client  or  (c)  to  meet  amounts  owed  by  the  client  to  the  Licensed  Corporation  or  the Associated Entity. Failure to observe sections 4 and 5 of the Rules, without reasonable excuse or with intent to defraud, is a criminal offence punishable on conviction with imprisonment and a fine. Other provisions of the Rules also carry criminal penalties under section 12 of the Rules.

In the interval between receiving client money and dealing with it in accordance with section 4(4) of the Rules, Licensed Corporations and Associated Entities are reminded that they hold the  client  money  as  trustee  and  have  a  fiduciary  duty  to  the  client  to  safeguard  the  client money  and  to  hold  or  use  it  only  in  accordance  with  the  client's  instructions.  Failure  to honour such fiduciary duty may expose a Licensed Corporation or Associated Entity to civil suit and liability to pay damages to the client.

Our Ref:  SFO/IS/28/2003

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

25 November 2003 Circular to Licensed Corporations and Associated Entities page 2

It  follows  that  Licensed  Corporations  and  Associated  Entities  should not  use  client  money during this interval for their own purposes, such as settling or reducing overdraft facilities, settling purchases of house investments or lending to a related corporation. Any such use of client  money  is  likely  to  constitute  a  breach  of  fiduciary  duty  and  is  contrary  to  General Principle 8 of the Code of Conduct for persons licensed by or registered with the Securities and Futures Commission. General Principle 8 provides that a licensed person should ensure that client assets are promptly and properly accounted for and adequately safeguarded. If a Licensed Corporation uses client money for its own purposes, its fitness and properness will be impugned, which may result in disciplinary proceedings under the SFO.

Licensed  Corporations  and  Associated  Entities  are  reminded  to  establish  and  maintain adequate internal controls to ensure that all client  money is adequately safeguarded and to prevent unauthorized and illegal use of client money.

Should you have any queries regarding the contents of this circular, please contact Ms Seine Luk on 2842-7696.
